class BytesIOCopy(io.BytesIO):
    """Patch ``io.BytesIO`` to let the written stream be copied to another.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def flush(self) -> None:
        super().flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return super().write(b)

    def fileno(self) -> int:
        """Raise a clear error instead of the confusing one from the
        base ``io.BytesIO`` implementation.

        Code invoked through :class:`CliRunner` sometimes passes
        ``sys.stdout``/``sys.stderr`` to APIs such as
        :func:`subprocess.run`, which require a real file descriptor.
        Since these streams are captured in memory during testing,
        there is no file descriptor available.

        .. versionadded:: 8.3.2
        """
        raise io.UnsupportedOperation(
            "The stream does not have a file descriptor because it is"
            " captured in memory by the test runner. To use a stream"
            " that has a real file descriptor, use"
            " ``subprocess.PIPE``, an open file, or a file descriptor"
            " directly instead of ``sys.stdout``/``sys.stderr``."
        )

class BytesIOCopy:
    """A binary stream backed by a real temporary file (so it has a
    valid file descriptor, unlike ``io.BytesIO``), whose writes are
    also copied to another stream.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2

    .. versionchanged:: 8.3
        Backed by a real file instead of ``io.BytesIO`` so that
        ``fileno()`` works, e.g. when used as ``stdout``/``stderr``
        for :func:`subprocess.run`.
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        self._file: t.IO[bytes] = tempfile.TemporaryFile()
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def flush(self) -> None:
        self._file.flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return self._file.write(b)

    def getvalue(self) -> bytes:
        position = self._file.tell()
        self._file.seek(0)
        data = self._file.read()
        self._file.seek(position)
        return data

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> t.Any:
        return getattr(self._file, name)
